title: Simply Wall St's Top Founder-Led Stocks to Watch in September: Paytm, Marico and Lenskart
excerpt: Founder-led Indian companies are back in focus as borrowing costs stay firm. Simply Wall St's September 2026 screen spotlights Paytm's profitability turnaround and UPI tailwind, Marico's copra-driven margin recovery, and Lenskart's post-IPO momentum.
body:
• Simply Wall St's September 2026 screen names three Indian founder-led stocks to watch: Paytm, Marico and Lenskart.
  • Paytm's Q1 FY27 net profit of ₹220 crore, up 79% year on year, got a fresh tailwind from NPCI's 0.4% MDR on large UPI transactions; Goldman Sachs estimates roughly ₹1,400 crore of incremental EBITDA in FY28.
  • Marico is banking on normalizing copra prices to revive Parachute volume growth, with Harsh Mariwala's promoter group targeting double-digit revenue growth.
  • Lenskart has climbed more than 58% in 2026 since its November 2025 listing as founder Peyush Bansal expands its eyewear footprint across India and overseas.

With the Federal Reserve pushing interest rates higher and cheap capital no longer doing the heavy lifting for equity returns, founder-led businesses are getting a second look as interest rates stay high: personal ownership tends to tighten capital discipline and sharpen long-term focus. Simply Wall St's September 2026 screen surfaced three such names: Paytm, Marico and Lenskart Solutions.

Paytm: the turnaround gets a policy tailwind

One97 Communications, best known as Paytm, runs a founder-driven platform linking payments, financial services and merchant tools. The business reports ₹89,670 million in revenue from data processing activities, entirely in India, with a market capitalization of about ₹1,184.6 billion, according to Simply Wall St. Founder Vijay Shekhar Sharma still shapes the product roadmap, capital choices and risk appetite.

"Continued rapid digitization of financial services in India and rising smartphone/data penetration are expanding Paytm's user base, especially in underserved Tier II/III and rural markets, which in turn supports higher transaction volumes and a larger addressable market."

— Simply Wall St, September 2026

Paytm reported a Q1 FY27 net profit of ₹220 crore, up 79% year on year, with revenue up 28% to ₹2,448 crore and record EBITDA of ₹203 crore at an 8% margin, per Outlook Business.

On September 16, NPCI announced a 0.4% merchant discount rate on person-to-merchant UPI transactions above ₹2,000, with person-to-person transfers remaining free. Goldman Sachs estimated an industry revenue pool of around ₹20,600 crore and roughly ₹1,400 crore of incremental EBITDA for Paytm in FY28 in a high-end scenario, CNBC TV18 reported. Paytm shares, up more than 30% this year, touched about ₹1,748 on September 9.

Marico: copra costs normalize, Parachute revives

Marico, the FMCG group behind Parachute, Saffola, Set Wet and Nihar, is a founder-influenced company where Harsh Mariwala's promoter group still anchors decisions on brands, capital use and expansion. It reports ₹143.47 billion in revenue — ₹108.68 billion of it in India — with a market value of about ₹1,040 billion, according to Simply Wall St.

"The normalization of copra prices following an unprecedented inflationary cycle is expected to drive meaningful recovery in Parachute's volume growth, as pricing stabilizes and Marico leverages its scale, supply chain, and market share gains, thus supporting overall revenue and future margin expansion."

— Simply Wall St, September 2026

Marico has guided for double-digit revenue growth, and Q1 FY27 delivered higher sales and earnings within that framework, per the screening. Management is pushing into premium haircare, health-focused foods and digital-first labels such as True Elements and Plix to diversify beyond the core franchises.

Lenskart: post-IPO momentum under the spotlight

Lenskart Solutions is a founder-led, tech-enabled eyewear retailer that designs, manufactures and sells branded glasses across India and overseas. It generates ₹96,338 million from medical optical supplies — ₹56,217 million in India, ₹40,729 million internationally — with a market capitalization of about ₹1,229.6 billion, per Simply Wall St. Peyush Bansal drives product design, brand building and omnichannel execution.

Lenskart listed in November 2025 at ₹402 a share, valuing the company at $7.7 billion after an $828 million IPO, Reuters reported. The stock is up more than 58% in 2026, though valuations were tested on September 21, when a ₹2,047 crore block deal — 3.53 crore shares, with Platinum Jasmine the likely seller — pushed it down over 3% to ₹683, according to The Economic Times.

Risks to the thesis

All three trade on premium multiples that demand flawless execution. Paytm's fortunes hinge on regulatory decisions around UPI economics and on containing partner and fraud risk. Marico's margin story needs commodity prices to stay calm — a fresh spike in copra or edible oils would squeeze the profit line the thesis relies on. Lenskart must prove cash generation matches the hype, with early investors still trimming.

What's next

Paytm's Q2 FY27 results will show whether the MDR tailwind pushes margins higher still. Marico heads into India's festive quarter with copra prices stabilizing — the test is whether Parachute volume growth materializes. Lenskart, past its first year as a listed company, faces scrutiny on store economics and international momentum. The full screening surfaced 116 more founder-led companies, but these three carry the clearest near-term catalysts into the final quarter of 2026.
